newsitem.title: UK: Zinc breaks higher on LME, hits 23-month peak.
newsitem.headline: Zinc breaks higher on LME, hits 23-month peak.

text.p: Zinc prices rose strongly during Wednesday afternoon London Metal Exchange (LME) trading, hitting the highest levels since February 1995.
Traders said renewed buying helped three months push above $1,123 -- the previous 10-month high. Business at $1,126 a tonne was $17 up from Tuesday.
Traders said zinc's strength reflected consistent stock declines, with the LME inventory now at its lowest level for four years, 61 percent below the October 1994 record of 1.24 million tonnes.
There has also been an influx of investment fund interest in base metals this year, with zinc a prime candidate as prices have underperformed in recent years.
So far this week prices have risen nearly $60. Traders said there was likely to be a profit-taking reaction before the market looked towards its next upside objective -- the $1,239 January 1995 high.
